evidence: app/src/lib/data.functions.ts:4 — every page's data flows through createServerFn/.validator(), which reached stable status only with TanStack Start 1.0 on 2026-10-13 (17 days before today)
app/src/lib/data.functions.ts:5,10,15,20,25 — .validator() is canonical only since 1.168.25 (June 2026); it replaced the deprecated inputValidator
app/vite.config.ts:6 — tanstackStart() plugin now requires Vite 8 (shipped ~2026), confirmed by the Start 1.0 stable release notes
app/package.json:9 — production serving via srvx, which itself only reached 1.0.x in the second half of 2026 (0.11.x as of July 2026)
grep of app/src for unstable|experimental|canary|preview|rc — zero matches outside generated routeTree.gen.ts and dist/
reach.rationale: Zero experimental/preview/RC/canary APIs, but the entire data layer rests on APIs that were release-candidate until two weeks ago, and the build/serve stack (Vite 8, srvx 1.0, TS 7) is all under a year old — squarely 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.functions.ts:1-26 — createServerFn is imported in exactly one file; all six server functions are exported behind named wrappers that routes consume (app/src/routes/index.tsx:12 imports getHomeData, not the framework API)
app/src/lib/api.server.ts:1-30 — server-only data logic isolated in a .server.ts-named module per the documented convention, so the framework seam is one file
app/src/routes/__root.tsx:12 — shellComponent, the other new-ish API, lives in a single root file
app/vite.config.ts:7 — the tsconfigPaths flag is one line in the config
app/package.json:5-13 — exact version pins (1.169.4, 1.170.46, 8.3.5) freeze the recently-stable stack against churn
containment.rationale: Every recently-stable API sits behind a one-file seam (the server-function wrapper module), which is exactly the documented .functions.ts/.server.ts organization; a change to any of these APIs touches one or two files, not many.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.functions.ts:4 — createServerFn is the framework's only way to load request-time data server-side, which the spec requires (data must be fetched over HTTP at request time, never at build time)
app/src/lib/data.functions.ts:5 — .validator() is used instead of the deprecated inputValidator, matching the June 2026 canonical API and avoiding compiler warnings
app/src/routes/__root.tsx:12 — shellComponent is the documented way to render the <html> shell in Start, replacing the older RootDocument pattern
app/vite.config.ts:7 — resolve.tsconfigPaths replaces the third-party vite-tsconfig-paths plugin, dropping a dependency
no usage of generateFunctionId, RSC, middleware, createIsomorphicFn, or any capability the docs mark experimental (grep: zero matches in app/src)
justification.rationale: Every use is the currently documented canonical API buying something the older stable alternative couldn't (server-side request-time fetching, non-deprecated validation, built-in path aliases), and the app steered clear of the one explicitly experimental option and all deprecated predecessors.

findings.issue: The entire data layer rides on server functions from a framework whose 1.0 stable release shipped only on 2026-10-13, so churn risk is inherent even though nothing is experimental.
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact version pins in package.json and preserve data.functions.ts as the single seam between routes and the framework; revisit when Start has a few more stable minors.

findings.issue: Production serving depends on srvx, which only crossed 1.0 in the second half of 2026 (0.11.x as of July 2026).
findings.suggestion: The pinned 1.0.8 matches the documented Start node-server convention, so this is fine; just keep the pin exact so CLI flag changes (--entry/--static) can't surprise a deploy.

findings.issue: typescript 7.0.2 — the brand-new native-compiler major — is a devDependency but no script ever invokes tsc, so the newest tool in the stack is also the least exercised.
findings.suggestion: Either add a `typecheck` script that actually runs it, or drop it since the Vite pipeline handles transforms independently.

summary: This is a conservative, current-stable codebase: zero experimental/preview/RC/canary APIs, no unstable flags, and it consistently chose the canonical non-deprecated variant of every framework API (validator over inputValidator, shellComponent over the old shell pattern, built-in tsconfigPaths over a plugin). The only experimentalness is recency — the mandated framework itself went 1.0-stable seventeen days ago and the whole data path flows through it. All of that new surface is contained behind a single 26-line wrapper module plus exact version pins, so breakage from upstream churn would be cheap to absorb.
